label: last copy step of length-3 sequences (t=5)
explanation: Active only in the copy phase and only on repeated inputs (in_first=0); never in the original or delimiter phase. The core is the final copy step of L=3 sequences (t=5, input = orig(1), output = orig(2)): about 11% of L=3 copy steps fire, holding ~61% of activation mass, and all top activations are of this kind (e.g. c u v <DEL> c [u]). Within this context, inputs u/i/h/b/v give the strongest activations while inputs such as a/g/k/l/w often stay silent (excluding them only trades recall for precision). The remaining ~39% of mass is a diffuse, weak tail in longer sequences, concentrated near the end of the copy phase (to_go 0-1, peaks at t=12 for L=7 and t=17 for L=9) on inputs h and i, but no simple predicate captures it cleanly. Dev F1 ~0.50, precision 0.57, recall 0.44, mass recall 0.61.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: h, i, u, r; t=12: h, i, n, u; t=13: h, i, n, m) and the token being output (most: h, j, i, n, 1, v; least: r, d, y, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=6.
